Q: Golang: set type struct to nil A:

The zero value of a struct value is not nil

Each element of such a variable or value is set to the zero value for its type: false for booleans, 0 for integers, 0.0 for floats, "" for strings, and nil for pointers, functions, interfaces, slices, channels, and maps.

In your case, this variable declaration var newVar Ptr creates the variable, binds corresponding identifier newVar to it, and gives it a type and an initial value.

Q: When iterating JavaScript object retrieves different values than shown when console.logged complete object A:

You cannot work with this anonymous structure. Your formaspago is not a defined variable or constant. In this case, you have to define the array as const and give it a name.

This is what you can do:

const array = [
    {
        "importe": 20000,
        "idformapago": "45",
        "ajuste": -2000,
        "precio": 18000,
        "cargo": "-10",
        "dolar": 0
    },
    {
        "importe": 20,
        "idformapago": "74",
        "ajuste": 29000,
        "precio": 29000,
        "cargo": "0",
        "dolar": 1
    }];

for (const element of array) {
   for (const key in element)
      console.log(`key: ${key}, value: ${element[key]}`);
   console.log(' '); // just to separate two array elements
}

Try it and see that everything is shown as defined.

Also, you don't really need to use Object.keys. The keys property could be useful if you only needed those keys. But as you are trying to output both keys and values, this property is excessive. All you need is the inner loop shown above.

In this example, you use a JavaScript object as a string-keyed map. In this case, the property names of the String type play the role of keys. For more advanced map, you can use the Map constructor. This is a very recommended approach in many cases. One important difference is that a Map instance can use any objects as keys, both objects and primitive values, and, most importantly, Symbol to guarantee the index uniqueness. A Map instance remembers the original insertion order of the keys.

Q: How do I clone a subdirectory only of a Git repository? A:

So I tried everything in answers to this question and nothing worked for me... It turns out that on version 2.24 of Git (the one that comes with cPanel at the time of this answer), you don't need to do this

echo "wpm/*" >> .git/info/sparse-checkout

All you need is the folder name

wpm/*

So in short, you do this:

git config core.sparsecheckout true

You then edit the .git/info/sparse-checkout file and add the folder names (one per line) with /* at the end to get subfolders and files

wpm/*

Save and run the checkout command

git checkout master

The result was the expected folder from my repository and nothing else.

Q: Create log file for errors in react A:

In a React web application, you cannot directly access the client's local filesystem to create a log file due to browser security restrictions. Instead, the standard approach involves logging to the browser's developer console during development or sending logs to a backend server or a third-party error tracking service in production.
